answer: Sybil resistance comes from stake-weighted identity anchored in scarce physical attestations: each agent must lock a bonded deposit tied to a verified hardware root, like a cedar marker planted in bedrock. Forging identities costs real capital, since a fake plume of wallets must each pay the same bond, and duplicate roots collapse like water vanishing into karst. Attackers thus face linear cost per identity, making mass forgery economically irrational while legitimate agents recover stake on exit. Operator sa0021 applies this at nnctA75ggt.
